insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -12.4% — Organic Install is behind most of it (-1,733, -12.3%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 27,062, against 30,896 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of -3,834. Where that came from: Organic Install -1,733 (-12.3%), Paid Install -1,353 (-9.4%), SEO Install -658 (-34.5%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (-1,733, -12.3%) and is now 45.5% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first. Known event: YCP iOS was delisted from the App Store on 2026-10-21 (因下架); its iOS Install / New User collapse is expected and its Install→New Subs conversion is an artefact. YCP accounts for about 81% of this change (-3,117).

insights.title: Next period outlook — Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing, mostly YCP.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -27.0% while App Total Install is -12.4% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-14.6pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days. Most of the fall comes from YCP (-54.4%); YCV is -16.0%.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -6.4% — down in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (-34.9%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 11-15 vs 11-08 is -6.4%, and App Total New Subs on 11-08 vs 11-01 was -34.9% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 11-15 vs 11-08): Subscription -8.1%, Pay as you go +24.1%. The drop was already visible in new subs a week ago, so lifting new subs now is what turns revenue around next week.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — App Total Revenue -5.8% — down mainly in Subscription (-5,667, -6.5%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 86,647, against 92,012 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-5,365). By purchase type: Subscription -5,667 (-6.5%), Pay as you go +302 (+5.6%). Pay as you go is 6.6% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YCP (-9.8%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YCP -3,153 (-9.8%, about 35% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in YCP -671 (-39.8%); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (20% of its revenue vs 6.6% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in US (-11.2%), while MX grows (+30.5%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is US -4,055 (-11.2%, about 39% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is MX +1,041 (+30.5%); Pay as you go moved most in JP +611 (+39.1%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (44% of its revenue vs 6.6% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — All App is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-27.0% vs Install -12.4%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: All App New Subs -27.0% vs Install -12.4% (worse than its installs); YMK New Subs -19.2% vs Install +0.1% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total Revenue (-11.1% vs -5.8%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total Revenue in US is -11.1% while all countries together are -5.8% — a gap of -5.3pp. US is about 39% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Market trend — JP is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-10.8%, now 10.6%).
insights.body: In JP, 10.6% of installs now turn into new subs — -10.8% versus last period. It is about 6% of revenue (a market worth watching): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.
